note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every sentence below is drawn from a Town of Apex page listed in this file. Apex states each court count in a published table and then repeats most of them on the venue's own page, so the numbers here are the town's twice over. Where it is silent, on surface, nets and fees at all five, the note says so rather than guessing.

slots.description:
Pleasant Park is the biggest pickleball site in Apex and the one to think hardest about before setting off. The town's court table gives it six courts, more than anywhere else in town, and its own page confirms "6 Pickleball courts" in the features list. It is also the only Apex venue the town marks as unlit, and the only one that publishes separate court hours: "Basketball and Pickleball Court Hours: Sunrise to 30 minutes after Sunset", against park hours of 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. So the largest concentration of courts in Apex is shut when the three smaller lit sites are still open.

One genuinely unusual thing: the town publishes a live court occupancy feed for the pickleball courts, which no other operator in this directory does.
slots.getting_there: 3400 Pleasant Plains Rd., Apex, NC 27502. The town publishes no parking capacity or restriction for the park, though its own FAQ list includes the question "Can I park along Pleasant Plains Road?". The answer has not been read here. Restroom facilities are on site and open from 6:30 a.m. with the courts and fields, an hour after the park itself opens at 5:30 a.m.
slots.what_to_expect: Six courts and no floodlights. Check the live occupancy feed before you drive out, then check the sunset: court hours here end thirty minutes after it, which in December is mid-afternoon. Nothing at this park can be booked. The town states courts cannot be reserved by players or groups, only by its own department for sponsored programmes, and that organised league play and private lessons outside town programming are not allowed per Town Ordinance. The town publishes no surface material for these courts, no statement about nets and no fee, so all three read "Not verified yet" rather than being filled in with something plausible.

faqs.a: No, and it is a verified no rather than a gap. The town's court table reads "No" in the Lights column, and the park's own page gives basketball and pickleball court hours as sunrise to thirty minutes after sunset. It is the only unlit pickleball site in Apex, and also the largest.

faqs.q: Can I check if the courts are busy before I go?
faqs.a: Yes, uniquely. Pleasant Park's page carries a live court occupancy feed for its pickleball courts. No other venue in this directory publishes real-time availability.

slots.description:
Kelly Road Park is a 25-acre neighbourhood park in Apex whose four pickleball courts are shared with junior tennis. The town's table lists it with four courts and marks it lit. The park's own features list puts it more precisely as "4 junior tennis / pickleball courts", which tells you what you are actually playing on: junior-sized tennis courts carrying pickleball lines, rather than courts built for the game.

Alongside them the park has one full-size tennis court, one basketball court, a lighted softball field, two playgrounds split by age, a picnic shelter with a grill, restroom facilities and a trailhead onto the Beaver Creek Greenway. It runs 6:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. year round, which together with the lights makes it a genuine evening option.
slots.getting_there: 1609 Kelly Road. The town publishes no parking guidance for this park, no lot, no capacity and no restriction, so the page simply does not say where to leave a car. Restroom facilities are listed among the park's features. The KidsTowne playground here was in the design phase of a renovation as of 20 August 2026, so there may be work on site, and no completion date has been published.
slots.what_to_expect: Four lit courts, shared with junior tennis, open 6:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. year round. Expect the sharing to matter: a junior tennis session has as much claim on the surface as you do, and with four courts a queue builds quickly at a neighbourhood park. Nothing here can be reserved. The town's policy is that courts cannot be booked by players or groups at all, only by its own department for sponsored programmes, and organised league play and private lessons outside town programming are not permitted under Town Ordinance. The town does not publish a surface material for these courts, whether nets are provided, or any fee.

faqs.q: Are the courts at Kelly Road Park dedicated to pickleball?
faqs.a: No. The park's own features list calls them "4 junior tennis / pickleball courts", and the town's table notes they are also used for junior tennis. You will be playing on a junior tennis surface with pickleball lines on it.

faqs.q: Can I play here in the evening?
faqs.a: The town marks this venue as lit and publishes park hours of 6:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. year round. It does not state what time the lights come on or whether they are switched or timed.

slots.description:
The Seymour Athletic Fields are the active half of Apex Nature Park, a site of over 160 acres that the town splits into two distinct sections with separate entrances. Section one, at 2500 Evans Road, is where the sport is: lighted tennis courts, lighted pickleball courts, lighted multipurpose fields, sand volleyball, a multi-age playground and a restroom. Section two, at 2600 Evans Road, is the quieter half, with an outdoor amphitheatre, a disc golf course, a dog park, environmental education stations and paved paths.

The town's court table gives the pickleball count as four, marks it lit, and notes the courts are also used for junior tennis. The park's own page confirms "Lighted pickleball courts" among the Seymour features but does not put a number on them, so the count here rests on the table.
slots.getting_there: 2500 Evans Road, and the entrance matters more here than at most parks. The town states there are parking lots at both entrances and a paved walkway connecting the two sides, so arriving at 2600 Evans Road for the pickleball means a walk across the park. A restroom facility is listed in the Seymour section, and a second one on the nature park side. Park hours run 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. year round, with the fields, courts and restrooms opening at 6:30 a.m.
slots.what_to_expect: Four lit courts shared with junior tennis, open 6:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. As everywhere in Apex, they cannot be booked: the town states courts are not reservable by players or groups, only by its department for sponsored programmes, and organised league play and private lessons outside town programming are not allowed per Town Ordinance. The town publishes no surface material for these courts, no statement about nets and no fee.

faqs.q: Which entrance do I want for the pickleball courts?
faqs.a: 2500 Evans Road, the Seymour Athletic Fields entrance. The other entrance, at 2600 Evans Road, opens onto the nature park side with the dog park, disc golf and amphitheatre. The town says there are parking lots at both and a paved walkway connecting them.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there?
faqs.a: Four, from the town's court table, which also notes they are used for junior tennis. The park's own page confirms the courts exist and are lit but does not give a number.

slots.description: Apex Community Park is the town's big general-purpose park, 160 acres with a lake of over 50 acres, and its pickleball is the smallest of the four outdoor sites at three courts. What it gives up in number it gains in certainty and in light. The park's own features list states "3 lighted pickleball courts" in a single line, which is the most direct statement of both count and lighting anywhere in Apex, and the town's court table agrees. The courts sit in a park that also carries tennis, basketball, sand volleyball, street hockey, ball fields and more than three miles of trails.
slots.getting_there: 2200 Laura Duncan Road for the park entrance. No parking capacity or restriction is published. Restroom facilities are on site, and park hours are 6:30 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. year round. A renovation of the playground next to the baseball fields was in its design phase as of 20 August 2026, adding ADA-accessible ramps and walkways to the adjacent parking lots, with no completion date announced.
slots.what_to_expect: Three lit courts, open until 10 p.m. year round, in a park with a great deal else going on. Three courts is few enough that a busy evening will mean waiting, and there is no way to shorten the wait by booking: the town states courts cannot be reserved by players or groups, only by its own department for sponsored programmes, and bans organised league play and private lessons outside town programming under Town Ordinance. What the town does not publish here is a surface, a statement about nets, or a fee.

faqs.a: The park entrance at 2200 Laura Duncan Road. The park publishes a second entrance, the Lake Trail entrance at 1808 Lake Pine Drive, which serves the lake and trails rather than the courts.

faqs.q: What else is at this park?
faqs.a: A great deal: six tennis courts, two basketball courts, three sand volleyball courts, two street hockey rinks, three ball fields with batting cages reserved for league play, a fitness course, playgrounds, restrooms, over three miles of trails, and a 50-plus acre lake with an accessible fishing dock and a vessel launch.

slots.description:
The John M. Brown Community Center holds the first indoor pickleball courts verified anywhere in this directory. Four of them, on the Town Hall campus at 53 Hunter Street, and the town's court table marks them Indoor and lit. It also attaches the restriction that defines the venue: they are "available only for ages 55+, during designated open gym hours". This is not a drop-in gym for everyone, and the town publishes a separate Senior 55+ Indoor Pickleball Calendar for what hours those are.

The facility was formerly known as the Apex Community Center. The building itself is a rentable community centre with three large rooms separated by partition walls, an arts and crafts room and a catering kitchen, with rates from $24 to $101 an hour depending on the room, the day and whether you live in Apex.
slots.getting_there: 53 Hunter Street, on the Town Hall Campus. The town publishes no parking guidance specific to the centre and no restroom flag that could be verified, though it is a staffed public building with rentable rooms. The building's own opening hours are Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 9 p.m., Saturday 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Sunday 1 p.m. to 6 p.m., closed on Sundays from June through Labor Day.
slots.what_to_expect: Indoor pickleball, if you are 55 or over and you come at the right time. The building's hours are known, but pickleball runs "during designated open gym hours", which is a subset of them, so no court hours are published here. Check the Senior 55+ Indoor Pickleball Calendar the town publishes for this facility before travelling. As everywhere in Apex, the courts cannot be reserved by players or groups. The town publishes no surface material, no statement about nets and no fee for the pickleball itself.

faqs.a: Players aged 55 and over, during designated open gym hours. That restriction comes from the town's own court table, and it publishes a separate Senior 55+ Indoor Pickleball Calendar for the schedule.

faqs.q: Were these really the first verified indoor courts on this site?
faqs.a: Yes, at the time of writing. Every other venue in this directory is outdoors. Raleigh runs indoor open play at thirteen community centres and Cary rents three indoor courts at Middle Creek, but neither publishes what is needed here: Raleigh gives no per-centre court count and Cary gives no street address.
